title: See a few of my reviews below!  —Camping: @Joe Weinberg  —Girl Interr...
transcript: Here are my top 10 favorite shows I've seen in the first half of 2026, in alphabetical order. First I have Camping, which is still running, by the way, through July 12th. Taking place in the same tent over many years, it's about a pair of best friends who may or may not be something more. Possibly the hardest I've laughed this year was in Derangements by Nadja Leonhard-Hooper. This is a really absurdist play about a pair of friends who go to dinner. Something very strange happens that triggers a bizarre series of events. If you miss this one, I might recommend checking out the musical Hole, which is coming back next year, and it's co-written by the playwright of this play. Next I have Dirt, which was like part interactive theater, part game. The concept is that the East River suddenly fills in one day and you are tasked with building with your community to figure out what to build there. By far my favorite musical of the year was Girl, Interrupted at the Public. This was a really divisive one, but it was very much on my wavelength and I found it extremely moving. Next I have Gooey's Toxic Aquatic Adventure, which played at Bushwick Starr and this was like a fantastical puppet musical. Somehow managed to be a genuinely feel-good show while also being a very sharp satire of capitalism and pollution and stuff like that. I have Jerome by John J. Caswell Jr. Which was about an older gay throuple. I just thought this was really emotionally rich and beautifully written. The transfer of the London hit KenRex, which is a true crime thriller. And while it maybe wasn't the most thoughtful portrayal of this subject matter, it was a pretty exhilarating theatrical experience. The Spelling Bee revival opened in 2025, but I saw it in 2026, so it counts. And I just love this show. I found it even funnier and even more moving than I did the last time I revisited it. I think this production very much does justice to it. Second to last alphabetical show I have on this list is Voyage Into Infinity. This was a performance piece by Narcissister, which was essentially a live Rube Goldberg machine, but it also had eerie, hypnotic music, and they were all kind of dressed as children's dolls. Finally, I have the revival of You Got Older, which I found deeply moving, hilarious. I was just so absorbed in these characters and their world and their story, and the acting was phenomenal. Even though this list is alphabetical not ranked, this still might be close to being my favorite show of the year.
classificationReason: Explicitly framed as 'top 10 favorite shows I've seen in the first half of 2026' — covers 10+ shows in list format (Camping, Derangements, Dirt, Girl Interrupted, Gooey's Toxic Aquatic Adventure, etc.) with no single primary focus.
